title: Brazil After the Fires
summary: Brazil, 2781. The front fought second has grown past holding. General Ruggieri brings the colonists out to the ships.

labels.south: THE SOUTHERN ROAD: at the crossing the swarm was fought first, so the city had a year. Its machines come down the highlands.
labels.river: THE RIVER ROAD: at the crossing the city was fought first, so the swarm had a year. It comes down the rivers.

sides.name: The Army of Brazil
sides.about: General Ruggieri and the army of Brazil: the line, the riders, two guns, the Powder Wagon and a Drummer; the militia; three groups of Brazil's people.

sides.name: The Fire Fought Second
sides.about: What the army fought second at the crossing: the swarm on the river road, or the city's machines on the southern road.

objectives.text: BRAZIL'S PEOPLE: bring them to the ships ({aboard} of {people_n} aboard). If fewer than a quarter are aboard when the ships sail, the army has failed them.
The harbour fort at the port must stand: the ships load under its guns.
THE FORD: hold the ford with the line and the guns. The outposts on the far side are falling back across it. The front breaks in {clock:front}.
objectives.phone: Hold the ford: the front breaks in {clock:front}.

objectives.text: Cover the outposts' families as they come over the ford: {g1_in} of {g1_n} across.

THE COLUMN: the people walk to the coast by themselves, in three groups. Alone a group only walks; with your DRUMMER beside it (six tiles) it keeps the army's pace. Move him from group to group, and keep the line between them and the forest.
objectives.phone: Walk the Drummer beside a group: it keeps the army's pace.

objectives.text: THE REARGUARD: they come down the road behind the column. Leave a few men and a gun at the back.
THE PASS: they got ahead of you and hold the pass on the road ahead ({amb_left} left). The people stop before it: clear it and they go on. They will not wait for ever.
THE SHIPS sail in {clock:ships}. Hold the bluff before the quay; every group must be on the quay before then. The harbour's Barracks trains for you.
CATCH THEM ON THE ROAD: keep more than half of the people from the ships ({aboard} of {people_n} aboard so far), or break the harbour fort. More of yours come out every minute at the edge.
objectives.phone: Keep half of them from the ships: {aboard} of {people_n} aboard.

k_open1.text: Act three. It left Brazil in our own ships, in crates with our seal on them. But first Brazil itself.

k_open2.text: At the São Francisco you chose which fire to fight first. The other one did not wait for us.

k_open_s.text: The city had a year behind its walls. Ruggieri wrote to me from the southern road.

k_open_r.text: The swarm had a year on the rivers. Ruggieri wrote to me from the river road.

r_open1.text: Brazil, 2781. I have commanded this army for eleven years. This was the first order I gave to go backwards.

r_open_s.text: The machines came out of Concórdia in the spring. The valley's people had one road, down the highlands to Santos.

r_open_r.text: The swarm came down the rivers with the flood. The river towns' people had one road, down the Amazon to Belém.

k_open_f.text: Ruggieri wrote this down as it happened. Here is how it would have gone if the road had been theirs.

n_open_f.text: Brazil, 2781. A column of the Crown on the one road to the sea, with the people of a whole country walking in it.

r_1.text: We are a year too late for this country. We can still get its people to the ships.

n_lesson.text: Hold the ford with the line and the guns. The outposts on the far side are falling back across it with their families. There is no base here: the Powder Wagon refills the muskets.

n_fall.text: The outposts fall back toward the ford. Their families walk ahead of the soldiers.

s_op.text: General! The creek post is coming in. They are right behind us.

a_op.text: General! The batteries are coming in. The machines are out of the gates behind them.

n_chase.text: They come after the outposts' families. Send riders over the ford to cover them.

h_cover.text: Volunteers, at the water. Let the women and the little ones through first.

op_in.text: The outposts' families are over the ford.

r_wave.text: Canister. Let them come to the water.

t_fort.text: Fort Constantine's men are with you, General. We held one fort; we can walk one road.

h_vol.text: The Virginia Volunteers, General. My father's farm was saved by your guns. We owe you a road.

r_drum1.text: Boy, keep the drum going. They walk to it better than they walk to me.

r_fields.text: Father Tomasz left São Rafael's fields standing. Its people walk with us now, and they still sing at Vespers.

r_burned.text: São Rafael's fields were burned in '76. There is nobody from there left to walk with us.

r_thin.text: Some of their nests outlived the rains at Óbidos. Everything they laid since is on this river with us.

r_held_off.text: We only held Concórdia off last year. Its works never stopped. There are more of them than I left at its gates.

r_close.text: We blew its great spring last year. Whatever comes out of Concórdia now comes without its great engines.

r_barra.text: The Barra's lower town burned in '78. What garrison is left came down with Nazaré's people.

a_fought.text: The valley stood with you once against the machines, General. It walks with you now.

a_parley.text: Most of the valley stayed in their houses. They did not believe the machines would come down. A few of us came.

n_break.text: The front breaks. Leave the ford: the people set out for the coast in three groups.

r_break.text: That is enough. Guns limber up. Everybody walks.

n_lesson2.text: Alone a group of people only walks. Walk your Drummer beside a group and it keeps the army's pace. Move him from group to group.

n_drum_on.text: The drum sets the pace: the group beside it walks with the army.

n_slow.text: Without the drum the group falls back to a walk.

r_drum.text: Keep the drum where the children are.

n_raid.text: A raid out of the forest on the column. They go for the people.

r_raid.text: Riders to the flank! Do not chase them into the trees.

n_pursue.text: More come down the road behind the column.

n_group_in.text: A group reaches the port and goes down to the quay.

n_lost_group.text: One of the groups is gone. Nobody of it reached the ships.

n_ambush.text: They got ahead of the column: they hold the pass on the road ahead. The people stop before it and wait until it is clear.

r_ambush.text: Line, forward through the people. Clear the pass, or they walk into it.

n_pass_clear.text: The pass is clear. The people go on through it.

n_pass_late.text: The people will not wait any longer with the pursuit behind them. They go into the pass.

n_port.text: The port. The ships lie off the quay. Hold the bluff before it until they sail; every group must be down on the quay by then.

r_port.text: Guns on the bluff. The harbour's Barracks is ours: spend the treasury on men, it will not sail with us.

r_count.text: Count them aboard. All of them. I want the number for the King, not a guess.

n_all_aboard.text: Every group still walking is aboard. The last boats wait for the army: hold the bluff a little longer.

n_sail.text: The ships sail. The army goes down to the boats last, the guns spiked on the bluff.

n_fort_lost.text: The harbour fort is broken. No ship can load under the fire on the quay.

n_too_few.text: The ships sail with too few aboard. Most of Brazil's people are still on the road.

r_hurt.text: It is nothing. Help me onto the gun carriage and keep walking.

n_f1.text: Yours come out at the edge. The army holds the ford; its outposts are falling back across it with their families.

n_f2.text: When the front breaks the people walk to the ships in three groups. Catch them on the road.

n_f_reinf.text: More of yours come out at the edge.

n_f_break.text: The front breaks. The column leaves the ford for the coast.

n_f_port.text: The first of them reach the port. The ships sail before long.

n_f_won.text: The ships sail half empty. The people are still on the road.

n_f_lost.text: The ships sail full. The road to the sea is empty.

r_end_many.text: We brought most of them out. I have the number in my hand: {aboard} of {people_n}.

r_end_some.text: We brought some of them out. The rest are on that road still. I wrote the number down: {aboard} of {people_n}.

r_end_few.text: We brought too few of them out. I will carry that number to my grave: {aboard} of {people_n}.

r_end2.text: From the deck the coast looked as it always had. Green to the water. You would not have known.

k_end1.text: That was Brazil. We had held it for three hundred years, and we left it in a season.

k_end2.text: And by then it was already in the ships' holds, on its way to the rest of the world.

k_end_f.text: That is not how it went. Ruggieri brought them to the ships. But I have kept this page.

n_end_f.text: The ships sailed half empty, and the road to the sea stayed full.

new_band.text: NEW: THE DRUMMER. The army's drum: soldiers in his ring (five tiles) march a little faster, and his SOLO quickens them more for a few seconds. Here he does more: a group of Brazil's people with the Drummer beside it keeps the army's pace. The Armoury trains more where there is one.

rome.caption: Rome, the present. The King at the war map.

bluff.caption: The last bluff over the harbour.

text: Brazil, 2781. You are General Ruggieri and the army of Brazil: the line, the riders, two guns, a Powder Wagon and a Drummer. The front fought second at the crossing has grown past holding: bring the people out to the ships.

First hold the ford while the outposts fall back. Then walk the people down the road to the port in three groups: a group keeps the army's pace with the Drummer beside it. Last, hold the bluff before the quay until the ships sail.
At least a quarter of the people must be aboard, and the harbour fort must stand.
Brazil, 2781. You are what the army fought second at the crossing: the swarm on the river road, or the city's machines on the southern road.
A column of the Crown walks the people of a whole country to the ships. Keep more than half of them from the ships, or break the harbour fort.
